prompt: A ketone with molecular formula C₆H₁₂O (M⁺ = 100) shows a strong fragment at m/z = 58. What rearrangement explains the loss of 42?

options.label: McLafferty rearrangement — loses a propene (C₃H₆, 42 Da) via γ-H transfer
α-cleavage — releases a C₃H₇ radical (43 Da), giving the complementary acylium
Loss of water + ethylene — H₂O (18) + C₂H₄ (28) = 46, close to 42
Retro-aldol — splits the ketone into enolate + aldehyde fragments, losing 42

explanation: McLafferty: carbonyl with γ-H → 6-membered TS, γ-H migrates to O, α-β bond cleaves, releases a neutral alkene (here propene = 42). The remaining enol-form radical cation lands at m/z 58. α-cleavage would lose 43 (not 42) and gives an acylium. Textbook diagnostic for carbonyls with γ-H.
